verdict.rationale: Alacritty runs entirely on the user's own machine, so there is no vendor-hosted service to depend on. The docs show it can be built from source (`cargo build --release`, including feature-flagged Wayland builds) or installed via `cargo install` and package managers on Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows. The macOS Homebrew cask being disabled affects only one convenience install path, since building from source still works. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement in the evidence, and a working prebuilt-binary install path on macOS (currently source build or Gatekeeper bypass).
